newsitem.title: ALBANIA: SOCCER-ALBANIA LEAGUE HALTED DUE TO UNREST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ALBANIA LEAGUE HALTED DUE TO UNREST.

text.p: Albania's soccer federation said on Friday it had postponed all matches indefinitely until the interior ministry could guarantee security after a wave of unrest over a pyramid savings scheme scandal.
Albanian soccer federation secretary-general Eduard Dervishi said first division soccer club officials had decided to postpone further matches until peace had returned to the Balkan state.

"The championship is indefinitely postponed until the situation all around the country calms down," Dervishi told Reuters. "It was a unanimous decision and clubs said the federation should ask for confirmation that the situation is calm before resuming."
Dervishi said there was growing pressure from Germany and Ukraine to hold their World Cup group nine qualifying matches against Albania in another country.
Tirana hoped the home matches against Ukraine on March 29 and Germany on April 2 would go ahead but officials said they were still awaiting an answer from soccer's world governing body FIFA.

Sports events were halted a month ago when violent protests sparked by the collapse of pyramid savings schemes swept the country. Albania's soccer league leaders Flamurtari boycotted matches in support of protests in their home town of Vlore.

Demonstrators in Vlore, 150 km (90 miles) south of Tirana, some of who have lost their life savings in the investment swindle, have held daily peaceful protests in the Adriatic port town for the past three weeks.
Dervishi said a friendly under-21 soccer match against neighbouring Montenegro planned for next week may not go ahead as events in Albania appeared to be moving so fast.
The unrest caused the cancellation of a friendly against Macedonia last week as Skopje authorities refused to allow players to travel to Tirana.
